subdomain: 1.4 Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

en.question: A team is considering parallel research agents for a high-value market-entry study. It has not yet shown that multiple agents are preferable to one investigator. Which findings would strengthen the architectural case for separate workers? Select 2 answers.

options.text: The study contains substantial evidence-gathering branches that can proceed independently under clear assignments.
options.note: Independent branches allow useful parallel exploration without requiring every worker to share each intermediate decision. Clear assignments limit duplication and coverage gaps.

options.text: Every research decision depends on the complete, continually changing context held by all other workers.
options.note: Heavy shared context and dependencies increase coordination and consistency costs. They weaken rather than strengthen the case for separate workers.

options.text: Measured improvement in study quality or completion time justifies added token and coordination costs.
options.note: Economic viability depends on the value of the improvement, not on agent count. Evidence of sufficient benefit addresses the added operating cost of multi-agent work.

options.text: The team can create one worker per discovered webpage, regardless of whether those pages answer distinct questions.
options.note: A webpage count is not a task-decomposition strategy. Redundant or closely related pages can create overlapping workers without useful independent work.

references.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
